say.dc2a27b5c742.note: First words of the game. Low and close. A breath after 'burned low'; 'the ground is moving' plainly, not spooky.

say.3dcd3f3caa00.intent: tells the survivor the fire is no protection
say.3dcd3f3caa00.note: Two plain sentences; the second as plain as the first.

say.2b72fa1dd85e.intent: shows the ambush before it springs
say.2b72fa1dd85e.note: Three images, each given its own room; a pause before 'They were waiting.'
say.2b72fa1dd85e.beats: A wagon on its side, and the ditch beside it full of the drowned. One of them is still holding the reins. [beat] They were waiting.

say.4a0952027e25.note: Even; the last sentence slower: it turns to look at you.

say.0663505a2971.intent: the first dead you killed was a child
say.0663505a2971.note: Plain, the same pace throughout; the facts do the grief. No catch before 'twelve at most'; 'and new boots' no softer than the rest.

say.87080a48980a.intent: reads a dead man and his last words
say.87080a48980a.note: The book's three lines read as written words, each a little more unsettled than the last; 'singing in the water' nearly a whisper.

say.4e278cbc120f.intent: a dead man speaks to you alone
say.4e278cbc120f.note: The narrator's part only; the watchman says the quote.

segments.text: ...and for you alone, the dead man's jaw moves:
It shatters its own lamps when it charges. Make it charge.

say.1e2fc7986134.intent: the fight ends, something waits ahead
say.1e2fc7986134.note: The fight is over: a breath before it. Then water, and a cold blue light, plainly.

say.f1f67faea5fb.note: Plain; 'The graves are listening.' said as simple fact.

say.f67dd9f6e97c.intent: the Warden is seen for the first time
say.f67dd9f6e97c.note: A hush: one of his four whispers. A pause after 'in the ford'; 'with a lamp in its fist' plain.
say.f67dd9f6e97c.beats: Something lies in the ford [beat], larger than any man, with a lamp in its fist.

say.33579e176a7e.note: After the fight, unhurried; 'full of cold light' plain.

say.4d8a46e7502e.intent: the quake stops; the way is north
say.4d8a46e7502e.note: 'For now.' on its own, then a pause; the road north plainly.
say.4d8a46e7502e.beats: The ground goes still. For now. [beat] The road runs north, toward the Waystation.

say.3beaff2ef058.note: Dawn, plainly; 'then gold' given room, no warmer than the rest.

say.656db5d6ed09.intent: the ember fades and takes something of you with it
say.656db5d6ed09.note: The prologue's last word. Even and kind through the rules of it; then much quieter for the mother's face. 'not quite where you left it' almost tender, and wrong.

say.c4d495431666.intent: death will not take you yet

say.8c1f7c369819.note: A list of sensations, unhurried; 'News travels fast here.' plain.

say.a49e30d2ba1e.note: Plain; a slight lift on 'places the road forgets'.

say.6947705bd0e4.intent: a small human mark on the well
say.6947705bd0e4.note: Read 'M. + J.' as letters: 'em and jay'.
say.6947705bd0e4.say: The water is a long way down, and clean. Somebody has scratched M and J into the stone.

say.a5b99f61e011.note: The note read as written words: 'Keep the lights lit.' Then the initial: 'C.'
say.a5b99f61e011.say: Beside the old captain's stone, sunk in the nettles, a trunk the Watch forgot: ember shards, a purse, and a note. Keep the lights lit. C.

say.3ff82d4e2ac7.intent: the wolf cloak has damned you
say.3ff82d4e2ac7.note: The second sentence a shade quicker: every wolf is on its feet.

say.74fcfb5cdf24.intent: the Kerchiefs take you for a friend
say.74fcfb5cdf24.note: Tense first half, relaxed on 'go back to their dice'.

say.b76e3053dc5f.note: A hush: one of his four whispers. 'slow, patient, enormous' each its own beat; a long pause after 'Not breathing.'; 'Praying.' barely voiced.
say.b76e3053dc5f.beats: Under the silence you hear it, for as long as a held breath: slow, patient, enormous. Not breathing. [beat] Praying.

say.0b5e75f9dfa0.intent: the caravan was robbed, not eaten
say.0b5e75f9dfa0.note: Plain; 'Wolves do not drive wagons.' as simple fact.

say.e6c4fb3a8998.note: Short observations; a pause before 'Under the seat'.

say.20dc615919d1.intent: the trail leads to the ravine
say.20dc615919d1.note: Short; 'Toward the ravine.' a shade lower.

say.8e845892b699.note: A list, plainly; the last sentence slower.

say.52d0f1dfa274.intent: a wolf dead of no wound

say.84f6c2c74004.note: Short observations; a slight lift on 'the drag-marks of lamps' (a clue).

say.769a1c759f88.note: Tight and quick; 'Run.' short, not shouted.

say.384c340b6b6d.note: 'like an eye opening' slower; a pause before 'The door is listening.'
say.384c340b6b6d.beats: The fragment fits one notch of the seven, and under your hand the whole sigil wakes, violet, like an eye opening. [beat] The door is listening.

say.66cdbe61b828.note: The inscription read slowly as old written words; 'all empty' quiet.
say.66cdbe61b828.say: Old-empire script over the door. Here the Seventh Legion buried what it could not burn. Below it, a sigil with seven notches, all empty.

say.99be1ad2c25a.note: 'It hums against your teeth.' close and physical.

segments.text: The skull turns, very slightly, toward you.
It was never locked from the outside.

say.6e1fab16785e.intent: someone went in and did not come out
say.6e1fab16785e.note: The token a careful find; a pause before 'None coming away.'
say.6e1fab16785e.beats: Bootprints in the mud, fresh, going up to the door. [beat] None coming away. Trodden into one heel-print: a copper toll-token, stamped with three roads.

say.b40ac14379d8.intent: a treasure where wolves go to die
say.b40ac14379d8.note: Slow; 'cold as snow' no softer than the rest.

say.ca6fbefec176.note: Plain; the nails are the detail.

say.185a7c3f55e7.intent: Jory, freed, asks for his uncle

segments.text: Jory. Jory Coyle. Is my uncle... Is he...

say.f1bc8c3f22ed.note: Each stopping its own short sentence.

say.a4755c96100b.note: Level and quiet throughout, 'Most of them do not crawl far.' included.

say.26621b48a47e.note: Level; a pause before 'and then there is only the fire', said low.

say.0622cbb5851c.note: Quick on the fire, slower on the glade.

say.005625eee2b8.note: The effort, then slower on the glade.

dlg.greymuzzle.first.0.note: Still; a long pause after 'for a long time'; the last image very quiet.

dlg.greymuzzle.show.0.note: Plain and close; 'and cannot' after a small pause. It ends on him waiting.

dlg.greymuzzle.ally.0.note: 'He is not coming.' on its own, plain.

dlg.greymuzzle.again.0.intent: the Pack has turned its back

dlg.chid.relight.0.note: The Order's words said with care; the kettle line plain.

say.3869640818fe.intent: the Pack knows what you did
say.3869640818fe.note: Plain; the second sentence is fact, not reproach.
say.3869640818fe.was: They smell the blood on you before they see you. Maeca said none since you last slept.

say.060466d9cefd.note: The size given slowly, a phrase at a time. A pause before 'You watch it long enough'; the end flat.
say.060466d9cefd.was: The ground shivers. At the bottom of the pit lies something pale and segmented, bigger than a house, and — probably — dead.
say.060466d9cefd.beats: The ground shivers. At the bottom of the pit lies something pale and segmented, bigger than a house. It does not move. [beat] You watch it long enough to be sure, and you are not.

say.10bf2fd84dd3.note: Three words, the way you'd say them at a bedside before light: not a cheer, not an order, no surprise. The player has just died, and nothing in her voice says so.

say.c4c1c1ee88e3.intent: tells the price without naming it
say.c4c1c1ee88e3.note: The line the game turns on, and it must sound like nothing. The first rising cost twenty-six lives; every one since costs one, someone in the valley, and she knows it. Say it as plainly as the weather, the second sentence no heavier than the first: no warning, no irony, no comfort. The player should hear "it gets easier" every time until the stair, and hear the price on a replay.

say.9dc671546463.intent: lets the dusk call land on a memory she won't name
say.9dc671546463.note: Straight after the gate's call. It is her own words coming back to her from a stranger's mouth, and she says nothing about that: flat, a fact about doors. No ache, no weight on 'door'.

say.c8db02ffeab0.intent: marks the middle of the night
say.c8db02ffeab0.note: A clock line, heard mid-fight. Two plain facts; the lamp still lit is only a lamp.

say.977de4be60a3.intent: ends a night the survivor stood through
say.977de4be60a3.note: Tired and level. A small easing on 'the warmth comes back into your hands', no relief in the voice.

say.fda6ac6c6045.intent: she goes on into the dark
say.fda6ac6c6045.note: Two short sentences, the second no heavier than the first. Not a warning.

say.5cbd1ba39848.note: The quiet is the news. Plain; let the line end and stay ended.

say.1ad34f33a2b4.intent: shows the Kerchiefs' fires from far off
say.1ad34f33a2b4.note: One image, said as a fact: 'the way a town lights its windows' is plain, not pretty.

say.f9f2c5cad405.intent: something is wrong at the Dig
say.f9f2c5cad405.note: The wrongness is in 'all moving the same way'; don't lean on it. Level, like counting.

say.87df61b27292.note: A beat after 'has woken'. 'Its light is violet' plain, the color as a fact.

say.fdad90e14306.note: Plain, level: the ember coming up is weather, not alarm.

say.cddfb7c98244.note: Arrival. The second sentence is the threat; say it no faster and no louder than the first.

say.18e64cad88a1.intent: the first stage done; the next one waits
say.18e64cad88a1.note: Mid-fight, between stages. 'The rails are singing' is plain description.

say.a89cdacbc1f4.intent: shows the lamplings carrying the crates
say.a89cdacbc1f4.note: Mid-fight. Plain; the oddness of 'carrying a crate' is in the words, not the voice.

say.0f4d56f97d68.note: Mid-fight. A little slower on 'one after another', as if watching them come on.

say.8ea79d1dcdf1.note: The Dig's end. Plain and quiet; there is pity in the picture, none in the voice.

say.44a50d15b7fa.note: Arrival. 'And it smells wrong' plain, a fact noted, no shudder.

say.59a5da567e47.intent: the Pack falls quiet; a sick thing is near
say.59a5da567e47.note: Mid-fight. Let the quiet in before 'In the quiet'. 'Something in the brush coughing' plain.

say.1394532b178f.intent: the den, and the sick wolves in it
say.1394532b178f.note: Mid-fight. A beat before 'and in it'. 'Gray shapes that do not get up' plain; they are dying, and she won't say so.

say.648f54abf56c.note: Mid-fight. No build: the second sentence as level as the first.

say.54d6b6c86b5d.note: Arrival. The whistles are a fact; 'and another answering' a touch slower.

say.884076412b80.note: Mid-fight. 'Three whistles, and none answering' is the camp silenced; plain. 'Somebody very big' dry, no joke in it.

say.c12346388d1c.intent: the cage yard, and three graves
say.c12346388d1c.note: Mid-fight. The graves are the news: a beat before 'and three mounds of new earth', and no weight on it.

say.8f4acfe90f92.intent: the cage yard, one cage empty
say.8f4acfe90f92.note: Mid-fight. 'With nobody in it' plain; it is the fourth cage, and she doesn't say whose.

say.ed1ff5a67b8c.note: Mid-fight. 'The way they were taught' carries Ashford's soldiers in it; say it as drill, flat.

say.c52914d98baf.intent: the crates are gone; the camp falls back
say.c52914d98baf.note: Mid-fight. Three sentences, even; a beat before 'Then they part.'

say.cbc22a062d1e.intent: the camp falls back for its chief
say.cbc22a062d1e.note: Mid-fight. Even; a beat before 'Then they part.'

say.def83ed2ca1b.note: Arrival. A beat before 'On the stair'. 'Coming up in step' plain: the dread is in 'in step'.

say.9bf57b5df8e4.intent: the next stage: a bow at the hall's end
say.9bf57b5df8e4.note: Mid-fight. Plain; 'a great bow' is a size, not wonder.

say.a83f4948df17.note: Mid-fight. 'One after another' with three even beats; 'and the dead turn to face them' level.

say.4350b3e997df.intent: the vault's dead come to attention
say.4350b3e997df.note: The fight's end. A beat before 'all at once'; 'with one sound' last and plain.
